questions.question: All monetary transfers or kinds sent by migrants to their place of origin are called ______.
questions.questionHtml: All monetary transfers or kinds sent by migrants to their place of origin are called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is remittances.

Key Points

  • Remittances:
    • Remittances are usually understood as financial or in-kind transfers made by migrants to friends and relatives back in communities of origin.
    • These are the sum of two main components:
    • Personal Transfers in cash or in-kind between resident and non-resident households and Compensation of Employees, which refers to the income of workers who work in another country for a limited period.
    • Remittances help in stimulating economic development in recipient countries, but this can also make such countries over-reliant on them.

Additional Information

  • According to the World Bank’s Migration and Development Brief, India has become the world’s largest recipient of Remittances, receiving USD 87 billion (a gain of 4.6 % from the previous year) in 2021.
  • India is followed by China, Mexico, the Philippines, and Egypt.
  • The United States is the biggest source, accounting for over 20% of all Remittances.

Other monetary policy tools include Repo Rate, Marginal Standing Facility, Open Market Operation, Statutory Liquidity Ratio, and Cash Reserve Ratio.

questions.question: _________ refers to buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government.
questions.questionHtml: _________ refers to buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government.
questions.solution: Open Market Operations (OMO) involve a central bank's purchase or sale of government bonds to regulate money supply and interest rates. Buying bonds increases the money supply and lowers interest rates, while selling bonds reduces the money supply and raises interest rates. OMOs are key tools of monetary policy. Marginal requirement refers to banks' reserve requirements, unrelated to bond transactions. Closed Market Operations indicate no bond trading, and Moral Suasion is a non-coercive method used by central banks to influence financial behavior without bond trading.

questions.question: Which of the following unemployment types is the result of people voluntarily leaving jobs in search of better ones?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following unemployment types is the result of people voluntarily leaving jobs in search of better ones?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Frictional unemployment.

Key Points

  • Frictional unemployment occurs when individuals voluntarily leave their jobs to find better opportunities or jobs that are a better fit for their skills.
  • This type of unemployment is usually short-term and is a natural part of the job market.
  • It can be beneficial as it allows workers to find positions where they can be more productive and satisfied.
  • Frictional unemployment is often influenced by factors such as job search time, availability of information about job vacancies, and mobility of labor.
  • It is different from other types of unemployment as it is not caused by economic downturns or structural changes in the economy but by individual choices and job transitions.

Additional Information

  • Disguised Unemployment
    • Occurs when more people are employed than actually needed, leading to low productivity.
    • Common in agricultural and informal sectors where surplus labor doesn't contribute to additional output.
  • Cyclical Unemployment
    • Results from economic downturns and is linked to the business cycle.
    • Increases during recessions and decreases during periods of economic growth.
  • Structural Unemployment
    • Caused by changes in the economy, such as technological advancements or shifts in consumer demand.
    • Workers' skills may no longer match the job requirements, leading to longer periods of unemployment.

questions.question: Which curve examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes?
questions.questionHtml: Which curve examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes?
questions.solution: The Phillips curve examines the inverse relationship between unemployment and wage inflation in an economy, introduced by A.W. Phillips in 1958. Lower unemployment leads to higher wage inflation, while higher unemployment results in lower wage inflation. Other economic curves, like supply, demand, and indifference curves, represent different economic relationships and dynamics.

questions.question: Which of the following age groups is considered as working population or working age in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following age groups is considered as working population or working age in India?
questions.solution: The question focuses on identifying the working-age population in India, defined as 15-59 years. This group significantly contributes to economic growth. Policies like the Skill India Mission, employment programs (e.g., MGNREGA), and social security schemes focus on enhancing their employability, productivity, and overall well-being to maximize the demographic dividend.

questions.question: The central bank may ________ to discourage credit in the economy.
questions.questionHtml: The central bank may ________ to discourage credit in the economy.
questions.solution: When the central bank increases the bank rate, it becomes more expensive for commercial banks to borrow money from the central bank. This, in turn, reduces the amount of credit that commercial banks can offer to their customers, thereby discouraging credit in the economy.

questions.question: ________ unemployment refers to the time lag between jobs when an individual is searching for a new job or is switching between jobs.
questions.questionHtml: ________ unemployment refers to the time lag between jobs when an individual is searching for a new job or is switching between jobs.
questions.solution: Frictional unemployment refers to the temporary period between jobs when individuals are searching for new employment or transitioning between jobs. It naturally occurs in a healthy economy and is usually short-term and voluntary, driven by workers seeking better opportunities. Factors influencing frictional unemployment include job search duration, availability of job information, and personal circumstances. To reduce frictional unemployment, policies can improve job matching services, provide better labor market information, and offer training programs. In contrast, seasonal unemployment is due to changing demand for labor, technological unemployment from advancements, and structural unemployment from skill-job mismatches.

questions.question: In India, inflation is measured on the basis of ______.
questions.questionHtml: In India, inflation is measured on the basis of ______.
questions.solution:
• The Reserve Bank of India had adopted the consumer price index as its key measure of inflation in India since 2014.
  • The consumer price index is the measure of the average change over time in the prices of consumer goods and services purchased by households.
    • The percentage change in the consumer price index over a period of time gives the amount of inflation over that specific period.
    • Consumer Price Index in India is published by the Central Statistical Organization (CSO).
    • It is published monthly in India.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about unemployment in India: a) Seasonal unemployment is mainly found in urban areas. b) Educated unemployed people are mainly found in rural areas of India. c) Higher cropping intensity is desirable for reducing unemployment in the rural economy. Which of the given statements is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements about unemployment in India:

a) Seasonal unemployment is mainly found in urban areas.

b) Educated unemployed people are mainly found in rural areas of India.

c) Higher cropping intensity is desirable for reducing unemployment in the rural economy.

Which of the given statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Correct choice: c) Higher cropping intensity (greater number of crops grown in a year on the same land) can reduce rural unemployment by providing continuous work for agricultural laborers. Choice a) is inaccurate as Seasonal Unemployment occurs in rural areas due to monsoon-based agriculture, not urban. Choice b) is incorrect as Educated Unemployment is linked to urban regions with more education and job-seeking in industrial or service sectors.

questions.solution: The question identifies what is not a function of money. Money overcomes barter inefficiencies like double coincidence of wants, enabling smooth trade, savings, and economic calculations in modern economies.

questions.question: ______ is an economic scenario where a peculiar combination of low growth and rising inflation leads to high unemployment.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is an economic scenario where a peculiar combination of low growth and rising inflation leads to high unemployment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Stagflation.

  • Stagflation is an economic scenario where a particular combination of low growth and rising inflation leads to high unemployment.

Key Points

  • Stagflation:
    • The term was coined by lain Macleod, a Conservative Party MP in the United Kingdom, in November 1965.
    • Stagflation is a situation in which the inflation rate is high, the economic growth rate slows and unemployment remains steadily high.
    • With stalled economic growth, unemployment tends to rise and existing incomes do not rise fast enough, and yet, people have to contend with rising inflation.
    • So people find themselves pressurized from both sides as their purchasing power is reduced.

Additional Information

  • Causes of looming stagflation situation in India:
    • Reduced consumption
    • Volatile Oil
    • Decreased credit availability
    • Unemployment
    • Inflation

questions.question: Which of the following is a function of money? (A) Used as a store of value (B) Used as a measure of value (C) Used as a medium of exchange
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following is a function of money?

(A) Used as a store of value

(B) Used as a measure of value

(C) Used as a medium of exchange
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A, B, and C.

Key Points

  • Money has taken many forms through the ages, but money consistently has three functions: store of value, unit of account, and medium of exchange.
  • The most important function of money is that it serves as a medium of exchange.
  • In a barter economy, it was difficult to exchange goods since the exchange in a barter system required a double coincidence of wants.

 Additional Information 

  • Medium of exchange and measure of value are the two primary functions of money.
  • Money helps in maximizing consumers.
  • It helps and promotes saving.​​

OMOs are flexible and easily reversible, reducing monetary policy lags.

questions.question: Which of the following is Fisher's equation of exchange?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is Fisher's equation of exchange?

options.html: MV=PT​

questions.solution:
The correct answer is MV=PT.

Key Points

  • Fisher's equation of exchange is represented as MV=PT.
  • In this equation, M stands for the money supply in an economy.
  • V represents the velocity of money, which is the rate at which money circulates in the economy.
  • P is the price level, and T represents the total volume of transactions.

Additional Information

  • Money Supply (M)
    • The total amount of monetary assets available in an economy at a specific time.
    • It includes various components such as currency in circulation and demand deposits.
    • Changes in the money supply can influence inflation, interest rates, and economic growth.
  • Velocity of Money (V)
    • The rate at which money is exchanged from one transaction to another.
    • It indicates the efficiency of money in an economy; a higher velocity means money is changing hands more frequently.
    • Velocity is calculated as the ratio of nominal GDP to the money supply.
  • Price Level (P)
    • The average of current prices across the entire spectrum of goods and services produced in the economy.
    • It is often measured by price indices such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI) or the GDP deflator.
    • Changes in the price level reflect inflation or deflation in the economy.
  • Total Volume of Transactions (T)
    • The total number of transactions or the total quantity of goods and services traded in the economy.
    • This can include consumer spending, business investments, and government expenditures.
    • The volume of transactions is an indicator of economic activity.

questions.question: This underemployment is hidden in contrast to someone who does not have a job and is clearly visible as unemployed. Hence, it is also called ______.
questions.questionHtml: This underemployment is hidden in contrast to someone who does not have a job and is clearly visible as unemployed. Hence, it is also called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Disguised employment.
Key Points

  • Disguised employment refers to a situation where a person is employed but is not fully utilized or is working in a job that is below their skill level.
  • It can occur in various forms, such as part-time work, temporary work, or low-paying jobs, which do not fully utilize a person's skills and abilities.
  • This type of underemployment is often hidden or not easily noticeable, unlike unemployment, where a person is actively looking for a job but cannot find one.
  • It can have adverse effects on an individual's income, career growth, and overall job satisfaction.
  • Disguised employment is a prevalent issue in developing countries, where a significant proportion of the workforce is engaged in low-paying or informal jobs.

 Additional Information

  • The word "unemployment" describes people who are actively looking for work and are employable but are having difficulty finding it.
  • Cyclic unemployment refers to the unemployment that occurs due to fluctuations in the business cycle, where there is a decline in economic activity, leading to a decrease in demand for labor.
  • Frictional unemployment refers to the temporary unemployment that occurs due to the time and effort required to match job seekers with suitable job openings.
  • Open employment refers to a situation where there are job vacancies available, and employers are actively seeking to hire workers.

questions.question: ______ unemployment occurs with changes in economic activity over the business cycle.
questions.questionHtml: ______ unemployment occurs with changes in economic activity over the business cycle.
questions.solution: Cyclical unemployment results from business cycle fluctuations, causing high jobless rates. It is a normal cycle of economic growth's ups and downs that happens over time. Temporary cyclical unemployment is based on how long an economic downturn brought on by a recession lasts.

questions.question: What is the empirically fitted relationship between the rate of change of money, wage, and rate of unemployment known as?
questions.questionHtml: What is the empirically fitted relationship between the rate of change of money, wage, and rate of unemployment known as?
questions.solution: The Philips curve illustrates the inverse relationship between unemployment and inflation, introduced by A.W. Phillips in 1958. It suggests that lower unemployment leads to higher wages and inflation, presenting a trade-off for policymakers.

questions.question: The general target of the monetary policy is to ensure ______. A) price stability in the economy B) greater tax collections for the government C) employment generation in the rural areas
questions.questionHtml:
The general target of the monetary policy is to ensure ______.

A) price stability in the economy

B) greater tax collections for the government

C) employment generation in the rural areas
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only A.

Key Points
  • Monetary policy:-
    • It refers to the measures taken by the central bank of a country to regulate the supply of money and credit in the economy.
    • The general target of the monetary policy is to ensure price stability in the economy.
    • This means that the central bank aims to keep inflation low and stable, so that prices of goods and services do not fluctuate too much.
  • Inflation:-
    • It is a key concern for any economy, as it erodes the purchasing power of money and makes it difficult for people to plan their finances.
    • The central bank uses various tools such as interest rates, reserve requirements, and open market operations to influence the supply of money and credit in the economy and keep inflation in check.

Additional Information

  • Price stability:
    • Price stability means keeping inflation low and stable.

questions.question: Money multiplier uses which of the following monetary instruments for its calculation?
questions.questionHtml: Money multiplier uses which of the following monetary instruments for its calculation?
questions.solution: The question asks which monetary instrument is used to calculate the money multiplier. The money multiplier depends on the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), which determines the maximum money creation by banks. Higher CRR reduces the multiplier. Other options like repo rate and bank rate are monetary tools but unrelated to multiplier calculation.

It is also known as search unemployment and is based on individual circumstances. Seasonal unemployment occurs at particular times of the year, while technological unemployment is due to advancements in technology. Cyclical unemployment is a result of economic cycles. Frictional unemployment.

questions.question: Who is the regulator of Micro Finance Institutions in India?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the regulator of Micro Finance Institutions in India?

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct definition of bank rate?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the correct definition of bank rate?

options.text: It is the rate of interest payable by commercial banks to RBI
options.html: It is the rate of interest payable by commercial banks to RBI

options.text: It is the rate of interest payable by a scheduled bank at which RBI lends overnight.
options.html: It is the rate of interest payable by a scheduled bank at which RBI lends overnight.

options.text: It is the rate of interest payable by RBI to commercial banks
options.html: It is the rate of interest payable by RBI to commercial banks

options.text: It is the rate of interest payable by a consumer to commercial banks.
options.html: It is the rate of interest payable by a consumer to commercial banks.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is It is the rate of interest payable by commercial banks to RBI.

 Key Points

  • Bank Rate refers to the official interest rate at which RBI will provide loans to the banking system which includes commercial/cooperative banks, development banks etc.
  • Such loans are given out either by direct lending or by rediscounting (buying back) the bills of commercial banks and treasury bills. Thus, the bank rate is also known as the discount rate.
  • The bank rate is used as a signal by the RBI to the commercial banks on RBI’s thinking of what the interest rates should be.
  • When RBI increases the bank rate, the cost of borrowing for banks rises and this credit volume gets reduced leading to a decline in the supply of money. Thus, an increase in the Bank rate reflects the tightening of RBI monetary policy.
  • A decrease in the Bank rate reflects the loosening of RBI monetary policy.

Additional Information

  • Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):
    • The RBI (Amendment) Bill, 2006, empowers RBI to prescribe CRR–Cash that banks deposit with the RBI without any floor rate or ceiling rate.
  • Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR):
    • It is the ratio of a liquid asset, which all commercial banks have to keep in the form of cash, gold, and unencumbered approved securities equal to not more than 40% of their total demand and time deposit liabilities (ranges is 25‑40%).
  • Repo Rate:
    • It is the rate, at which RBI lends short-term money to the bank against securities.
  • Reverse Repo Rate:
    • It is the rate, at which banks park short-term excess liquidity with the RBI.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of intermediate goods?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is not an example of intermediate goods?
questions.solution: Medicine is not an example of intermediate goods. Intermediate goods are incomplete goods that go between raw materials and finished goods as productive materials for further refinement in the production chain. Capital goods are used to convert basic goods into finished goods. The drug is a finished item and does not require further processing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the scheduled public sector banks in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT one of the scheduled public sector banks in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bandhan Bank.

Key Points

  • Scheduled Public Sector Banks in India:
    • These are banks that are included in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
    • These banks are eligible for loans from the RBI at the bank rate and can also avail of other facilities like deposits and clearing.
  • Canara Bank, UCO Bank, and Indian Overseas Bank are all scheduled public sector banks in India.
  • Bandhan Bank is not a scheduled public sector bank in India, it is a private sector bank.​

Additional Information

Canara Bank 

  • It is a public sector bank that was established in 1906.
  • It has a network of over 10,000 branches and ATMs across India.

UCO Bank

  • It is also a public sector bank that was established in 1943.
  • It has a strong presence in Eastern India and has over 3,000 branches and ATMs.

Indian Overseas Bank

  • It is a public sector bank that was established in 1937.
  • It has a network of over 3,400 branches and ATMs across India.

questions.question: The minimum rate below which banks are not allowed to lend money except in cases specified by the Reserve Bank of India is called ________.
questions.questionHtml: The minimum rate below which banks are not allowed to lend money except in cases specified by the Reserve Bank of India is called ________.
questions.solution: The Base Rate is the minimum interest rate of a bank below which it cannot lend, except in some cases allowed by the RBI.It is the minimum interest rate of a bank below which it is not viable to lend. The base rate, introduced with effect from 1st July 2011 by the Reserve Bank of India, is the new benchmark rate for the lending operations of banks.

questions.questionHtml: Which of the following definitions best describes the concept of microfinance?

options.html: A microfinance institution is a company registered under the Companies Act, 1956, and engaged in the business of loans and advances and acquisition of shares/stocks/bonds/debentures/securities issued by the government.

options.text: Microfinance is a banking service provided to unemployed or low-income individuals or groups, who otherwise would have no other access to financial services.
options.html: Microfinance is a banking service provided to unemployed or low-income individuals or groups, who otherwise would have no other access to financial services.

options.html: Microfinance refers to providing banking services to individuals living in rural areas.

questions.solution: Microfinance involves offering financial services such as small loans, savings accounts, and insurance to individuals who lack access to traditional banking, particularly those in impoverished or rural areas. It specifically targets unemployed or low-income individuals. Other definitions, like describing the business structure of a microfinance institution, digital-only banks, or services solely for rural areas, are incomplete or incorrect representations of microfinance.

questions.question: People like small farmers and seasonal workers who regularly move in and out of poverty are categorised as _______.
questions.questionHtml: People like small farmers and seasonal workers who regularly move in and out of poverty are categorised as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is churning poor.

  • The churning poor are the ones who regularly move in and out of poverty (example: small farmers and seasonal workers).

Important Points

  • The occasionally poor are the ones who are rich most of the time but may sometimes have a patch of bad luck.
  • Those who are usually poor but who may sometimes have a little more money (example: casual workers) are grouped together as the chronic poor.
    • Chronically poor people experience deprivation over many years, often over their entire lives, and frequently pass poverty on to their children.
  • When the number of poor is estimated as the proportion of people below the poverty line, it is known as ‘Head Count Ratio’.

Additional Information

  • As per the report of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (released on 7 January 2020), the state per capita income of Goa is highest in the country followed by Delhi and Sikkim.
  • Bihar has the lowest NSDP per capita (INR at Current prices) Rs. 43,822 in FY 2018-19.
  • Per capita income of Goa is 3.01 times more than India's average and 7.18 times more than the poorest state Bihar.

questions.question: Tax rates on higher income groups have been increased resulting in __________.
questions.questionHtml: Tax rates on higher income groups have been increased resulting in __________.

options.text: reducing inequalities of income and wealth
options.html: reducing inequalities of income and wealth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is reducing inequalities of income and wealth.

Key Points

  • Increased tax rates on higher income groups are aimed at redistributing wealth more equitably within society.
  • This measure helps to reduce the income gap between the rich and the poor, fostering a more balanced economic structure.
  • It can lead to increased government revenues, which can be used to fund social welfare programs and public services.
  • Progressive taxation is a key tool in addressing economic inequality and ensuring that wealthier individuals contribute a fair share to the economy.

Additional Information

  • Progressive Taxation:
    • It is a tax system in which the tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases.
    • It aims to reduce the tax burden on low-income earners and increase it on high-income earners.
  • Income Redistribution:
    • It involves the transfer of income from wealthier individuals to those with lower incomes through taxation and welfare programs.
    • The goal is to reduce economic disparities and provide a safety net for the less fortunate.
  • Social Welfare Programs:
    • These are government initiatives designed to provide support to the needy, including unemployment benefits, food assistance, and healthcare services.
    • Funded by tax revenues, these programs aim to improve the quality of life for disadvantaged groups.
  • Public Services:
    • Services provided by the government to all citizens, including education, transportation, and infrastructure.
    • Funded through taxation, public services are essential for the overall development and well-being of society.

questions.question: Which type of tax acts as an automatic stabiliser in the economy?
questions.questionHtml: Which type of tax acts as an automatic stabiliser in the economy?
questions.solution: Proportional income tax is the correct answer as it acts as an automatic stabilizer in the economy, changing in response to income levels. Professional tax is levied by state governments in India on individuals earning income through professions, trades, callings, or employment. Wealth tax is a tax on an individual's net wealth or assets, while capital gains tax is a tax on the profit earned from the sale of an asset.

questions.question: As per the recommendations of the National Statistical Commission, the Base Year of the GDP Series in India was revised from 2004-05 to _____ with effect from January 2015.
questions.questionHtml: As per the recommendations of the National Statistical Commission, the Base Year of the GDP Series in India was revised from 2004-05 to _____ with effect from January 2015.
questions.solution: The base year for India's GDP calculation was revised to 2011-12, effective January 2015, based on National Statistical Commission recommendations. This update, managed by the CSO, aligns economic metrics. Plans for further revision to 2017-18 are underway. The CPI base year is 2012, reflecting ongoing efforts to refine statistical accuracy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method used for measuring unemployment in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a method used for measuring unemployment in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Unusual Status Approach.Key Points

  • Methods used for measuring unemployment in India are the Weekly status Approach, Daily status Approach and Usual Status Approach.
  • These measures enable the existing unemployment rate in the economy for quantification and hence helps in taking remedial steps.
  • Based on time and willingness criteria unemployment mainly open unemployment and underemployment have been estimated using the following 3 approaches headed by Prof. M L. Dantwala.
  • Various reasons leads to unemployment which can vary from seasonal to technological advancements, and hence requires diverse measures to estimate the presence of unemployment in the economy.
  • The daily status approach is an inclusive and accurate measure to estimate unemployment because it takes into account the informal workers such as those engaged in agriculture.

Additional Information

  • The Weekly status Approach measures unemployment with respect to one week. 
  • In Daily status Approach, unemployment status of a person is measured for each day in a reference week.
  • Usual status approach measures the number of persons who remained unemployed for a major part of the year and gives the lowest estimates of unemployment.

questions.question: Which measure(s) is the Reserve Bank most likely to take to combat inflation in the economy? A) Increase repo rate B) Increase money supply C) Decrease cash reserve ratio
questions.questionHtml:
Which measure(s) is the Reserve Bank most likely to take to combat inflation in the economy?

A) Increase repo rate

B) Increase money supply

C) Decrease cash reserve ratio
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only A.

Key Points

  •  Increase repo rate:
    • This is the rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the Reserve Bank.
    • By increasing the repo rate, the Reserve Bank makes it more expensive for banks to borrow money, which reduces the amount of money in circulation and helps to control inflation.

questions.question: What does the government do in a contractionary fiscal policy for lowering inflation?
questions.questionHtml: What does the government do in a contractionary fiscal policy for lowering inflation?

options.text: Reduce the quantum of money by decreasing taxes and increasing spending
options.html: Reduce the quantum of money by decreasing taxes and increasing spending

options.text: Increase the quantum of money by raising taxes and reducing spending
options.html: Increase the quantum of money by raising taxes and reducing spending

options.text: Increase the quantum of money by decreasing taxes and increasing spending
options.html: Increase the quantum of money by decreasing taxes and increasing spending

options.text: Reduce the quantum of money by raising taxes and reducing spending
options.html: Reduce the quantum of money by raising taxes and reducing spending

questions.solution:
The correct answer is to Reduce the quantum of money by raising taxes and reducing spending.

Key Points

  • Contractionary monetary policy occurs when a nation's central bank raises interest rates and decreases the money supply.
    • It's done to prevent inflation.
  • The long-term impact of inflation can be more damaging to the standard of living than a recession.
  • Expansionary monetary policy boosts economic growth by lowering interest rates.
    • It's effective in adding more liquidity in a recession.

Additional Information

  • The benefit of monetary policy is that it works faster than fiscal policy.
  • The Federal Reserve votes to raise or lower rates at its regular Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
  • It takes about six months for the added liquidity to work its way through the economy.

questions.question: Which of the following has universal acceptability in discharge of debt & payment obligations?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following has universal acceptability in discharge of debt & payment obligations?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Legal tender money.

Key Points

  • Legal tender money is money that must be accepted if offered in payment of a debt.
  • It is recognized by the law of the land as a valid form of payment.
  • In most countries, the central bank or government issues legal tender money.
  • Examples include coins and banknotes issued by a central authority.
  • Legal tender money is backed by the government and is universally accepted within the country.
  • It is essential for economic stability and functioning of the financial system.

 Additional Information

  • Bonds
    • Bonds are debt securities issued by entities such as governments, municipalities, and corporations.
    • They represent a loan made by an investor to the issuer.
    • Bonds pay periodic interest and return the principal at maturity.
    • They are not universally accepted for payment of debts and obligations.
  • Houses
    • Houses are tangible assets and real estate properties.
    • They can be used as collateral for loans but are not a form of money.
    • Houses are not accepted for settling debts in a direct transaction.
  • Landed property
    • Landed property refers to land and any buildings on it.
    • It can be a valuable asset but is not considered a medium of exchange.
    • Landed property is not universally accepted for debt repayment.
